newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela cautiously welcomes Clinton's Africa plan.
newsitem.headline: Mandela cautiously welcomes Clinton's Africa plan.

text.p: ATLANTIS, South Africa, June 19 - South African President Nelson Mandela on Thursday cautiously welcomed U.S. President Bill Clinton's plan to encourage economic growth in Africa.
Mandela, the continent's most respected statesman, told reporters that unconditional help for Africa would be welcome.

"We welcome every attempt to help Africa to assert itself, but of course we don't accept any conditions and we do not think that it is in the interests of Africa for any people to supply us with assistance with conditions," he said.
"But any assistance which enables the continent of Africa to develop like other continents, we welcome."
U.S. President Bill Clinton announced a trade and economic development plan for Africa on Tuesday, which would include reducing tariffs for countries reforming their economies.

Clinton administration officials said the U.S. president would work towards a coordinated international effort -- including urging the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund to provide debt relief for poor countries.

Under the plan, the poorest countries in Africa would receive duty-free access for some 1,800 additional products, while any nation "undertaking concerted reforms" for their economies would benefit from reduced tariffs.

Administration officials said around 30 countries in Africa grew at more than five percent last year and a few reached a 10 percent growth rate. The IMF forecasts 4.7 percent growth for Africa as a whole this year.

The World Bank says that 37 out of 48 sub-Saharan African countries are undertaking serious economic reforms, including dismantling trade barriers, privatising state enterprises and easing investment laws.
